issue_request: FHIR-7538 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification ITS change request from the 2015 May core ballot asking the XML format page to clarify whitespace handling for value attributes, specifically whether XML schema whitespace processing applies or implementations should strip leading/trailing whitespace when writing and reading.
initial_application: The Jira resolution directed a Postel's-law note saying implementers should trim whitespace before writing and when reading. Jira records svn revision 6674, and git-svn commit a8566ea065d07d44c6a49ebb58bdd6e478b1a8a0 added that note to source/xml.html. Later commit a5c90c3db3cc87902faf8b096c1fdc5f179853fc added a datatypes.html link to xml.html#whitespace and changed the XML note to include an anchor, but the anchor was misspelled as "whitepace".
additional_context: The current source still contains the requested XML whitespace guidance and a related datatype note pointing readers to xml.html#whitespace. source/xml.html is a current core XML format page linked from the active documentation and resource-format pages, and source/datatypes.html is the current datatype narrative. No relevant Zulip or Confluence discussion was found, and the combined branch did not already contain an Issue-Reconcile-Key: FHIR-7538 audit commit.
reconciliation: Changed source/xml.html to rename the XML whitespace note anchor from "whitepace" to "whitespace". This fixes the broken intra-spec link without changing the normative wording, because the requested clarification was already present.
source_changes: source/xml.html: changed the XML whitespace note anchor from name="whitepace" to name="whitespace" so the source/datatypes.html link to xml.html#whitespace resolves.
